extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and counsel preparing AIA trial petitions (IPR/PGR) for the PTAB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and minimum procedural/substantive requirements for preparing and filing petitions requesting AIA trial proceedings (e.g., IPR/PGR) before the PTAB, including content, service, timing, evidence, and claim construction obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition as the vehicle to initiate AIA trial proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA trial proceedings at the Board begin with the filing of a petition that lays out the petitioner’s grounds and supporting evidence for the requested proceeding; other requests for relief must be in the form of a motion. (37 C.F.R. § 42.20(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the petition itself presents the grounds and supporting evidence; do not attempt to request substantive relief via informal filings—other relief belongs in motions under the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure timely filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely filing of the petition is critical to avoid statutory bars (e.g., the one-year bar) and to preserve the desired filing date (corrections may be given the date of the corrected petition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay special attention to statutory deadlines (one-year bar, prior civil actions) because corrections may change your effective filing date and thus affect eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with applicable content rules (e.g., 37 CFR 42.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete petition must comply with the content provisions of the rules (for IPRs, 37 CFR 42.104).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each required content element listed in the rule (see separate metrics for the five 42.104(b) elements). Noncompliance can prevent obtaining an initial filing date or lead to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper service prior to filing (37 CFR 42.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must have been properly served before filing in accordance with 37 CFR 42.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correspondence address of record for the subject patent or any other address known to the petitioner as likely to effect service. Check service requirements carefully because improper service can jeopardize the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify real parties-in-interest (35 U.S.C. 312(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must identify real parties in interest (RPIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately naming RPIs helps the Board assess conflicts of interest and estoppel. This is fact-intensive—err on the side of disclosure and name entities that would be subject to estoppel or preclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay required fees (37 CFR 42.15; 37 CFR 42.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must be accompanied by appropriate filing fees as required by the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current fee schedules and include payments to avoid delays or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for standing certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must certify the patent is eligible for IPR/PGR and that the Petitioner is not barred or estopped from challenging patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit certification statements addressing eligibility and any potential bars or estoppel; failure to certify properly can lead to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the challenge and precise relief requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must state the precise relief requested and identify the challenge being made to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state which claims are challenged and what specific relief (e.g., cancellation of specified claims) the petitioner seeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the challenged claims (37 CFR 42.104(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must identify the challenged claims of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List claim numbers clearly and unambiguously; treat each claim addressed as a discrete item of analysis elsewhere in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify statutory grounds and relied-upon patents/printed publications (37 CFR 42.104(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim challenged, the petition must state the specific statutory grounds under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 or 103 and the patents or printed publications relied upon for each ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie each ground to the supporting reference(s); be precise about which reference supports which ground for which claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: State claim construction and, for 112(f) terms, identify corresponding structure (37 CFR 42.104(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must state how the challenged claim is to be construed; where a claim contains a means-plus-function or step-plus-function limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the construction must identify the specific portions of the specification that describe the structure, material, or acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a discrete claim construction section for disputed/important terms and provide support (specification citations). For 112(f) claims, map functions to specification disclosure explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how the construed claim is unpatentable and map claim elements to prior art (37 CFR 42.104(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must explain how the construed claim is unpatentable under the identified statutory grounds and must specify where each element of the claim is found in the relied-upon prior art patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide element-by-element analysis with clear citations to the prior art; failure to map elements will weaken the petition and may lead to exclusion or no weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide exhibit numbers and explain relevance; identify specific portions of evidence (37 CFR 42.104(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must include the exhibit number(s) of the supporting evidence and the relevance of the evidence to the challenge, including identifying specific portions of the evidence that support the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which parts of an exhibit support which portions of your argument. The Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where a party fails to state relevance or identify specific portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and expert testimony must disclose underlying facts/data (Fed. R. Evid. 705; 37 C.F.R. § 42.65)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits expressing an expert opinion must disclose the underlying facts or data upon which the opinion is based; opinions without disclosed underlying facts/data may be given little or no weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the data, test methods, and underlying facts supporting expert opinions. Beyond the required disclosures, provide any additional information that will help the Board understand the significance of tests or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and certification regarding prior civil actions (35 U.S.C. 315)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner or real party-in-interest cannot have filed a civil action challenging the validity of a claim of the patent before filing the petition (35 U.S.C. § 315(a)(1)), with limited exceptions; the one-year time bar under § 315(b) applies from service of an infringement complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether any prior or parallel civil actions trigger bars or exceptions (e.g., counterclaims, DJ for noninfringement). Note that filing corrections may alter the operative filing date, which is critical if near the one-year bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify all interested parties, related matters, and counsel (37 CFR 42.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory notices must provide identification of real parties-in-interest, related matters, lead and back-up counsel, and service information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose related proceedings and entities that might be subject to estoppel or preclusion. Because RPI/privy determinations are fact-specific, provide thorough identification to avoid later disputes or time-bar problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid improper usage of claim charts
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim chart is a common way to specify where each element of a claim is found in prior art (per 37 C.F.R. § 42.104(b)(4)), and claim charts may use single spacing (42.6(a)(2)(iii)), but petitioners must not misuse the chart format to hide necessary argumentation or insert claim constructions and unpatentability arguments improperly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claim charts for element-to-reference mapping only; do not bury substantive construction or legal reasoning inside chart formatting to game page limits. Follow USPTO guidance and FAQs on acceptable chart use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly set forth any claim constructions and identify parallel constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to expressly set forth claim construction of disputed or important claim terms in a claim construction section is a common error; petitioner must include a statement identifying how a claim term is to be construed and support for that construction. If a parallel proceeding has a specific construction, identify it for the Board’s consideration (CTPG, 47; 37 CFR 42.100(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a dedicated claim construction section, cite support, and flag any relevant constructions from parallel proceedings. After filing, respond to new constructions raised by the Patent Owner, but do not raise new claim construction issues in the reply that were not previously presented.
